notes:
Task and constraints: Count words that can be stretched to match S by expanding sufficiently long repeated-character runs.
Idea: Run-length encode S and each candidate word, then compare the character sequences and counts.
Technique and why it applies: A run may expand only when the target count is at least three; otherwise counts must match exactly. itertools.groupby constructs the run encoding.
Invariant: R and count describe the target's run characters and lengths; each candidate is checked against them.
Edge cases: RLE returns a zip iterator, which can be consumed only once; the code stores and reuses it across candidates, so after the first comparison it may be exhausted.
Complexity: Run encoding and checks are linear in total characters, but iterator exhaustion makes the implementation incorrect for multiple words.

Task and constraints: Decide whether the first player wins the chalkboard game where each move removes a nonzero number and the remaining XOR determines the outcome.
Idea: Apply the known parity characterization: the first player wins if the total XOR is zero or the number of elements is even.
Technique and why it applies: When XOR is zero, the first player has no winning move; with an even count and nonzero XOR, a winning strategy exists under the game's rules.
Invariant: The reduction computes the XOR of all array elements and combines it with the array-length parity.
Edge cases: functools and operator are used without imports in the snippet, so it requires those names externally. Empty input reduces to the identity only if reduce receives an initializer, which it does not here.
Complexity: XOR reduction is O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Task and constraints: Determine whether the first player wins the chalkboard XOR game.
Idea: Compute the XOR of all values and test whether it is zero or the array length is even.
Technique and why it applies: This condition is the game's mathematical winning criterion, avoiding simulation of every possible move.
Invariant: reduce(xor, nums) is the XOR aggregate of the input.
Edge cases: An empty nums list raises an error because reduce has no initializer; the standard problem generally supplies at least one value.
Complexity: The reduction takes O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Task and constraints: Count visits to each domain and every parent subdomain from records containing a count and full domain.
Idea: Split each domain into labels and accumulate the count for every suffix domain.
Technique and why it applies: Walking labels from right to left constructs the top-level domain, then each progressively longer parent domain. The dictionary combines repeated visits.
Invariant: output maps each domain suffix to the total visits reported for all input domains beneath it.
Edge cases: The implementation prints intermediate lists and domains, creating unwanted debug output. It parses each record using a single-space split, which is less robust than split() for repeated whitespace.
Complexity: Processing T domain labels takes O(T) time and O(U) storage for U distinct suffixes.

Task and constraints: Return visit counts for every domain and each of its parent subdomains.
Idea: Split each domain into labels and build suffixes from right to left, accumulating counts in a defaultdict.
Technique and why it applies: Each parent domain receives the visit count of the full domain. defaultdict(int) supplies zero for previously unseen suffixes.
Invariant: result[domain] equals the sum of visit counts for all records contributing to that domain.
Edge cases: Input records are parsed by whitespace splitting, handling multiple spaces. Output order follows dictionary insertion order and is not otherwise constrained.
Complexity: The work is linear in total domain-label length, with O(U) storage for distinct subdomains.

Task and constraints: Find the largest area among triangles formed by any three input points.
Idea: Enumerate every three-point combination and compute its area using the determinant formula.
Technique and why it applies: The absolute cross-product expression gives twice the triangle area, so the code multiplies by one half and keeps the maximum.
Invariant: maxA is the largest area among triples examined so far.
Edge cases: Collinear points yield zero area. If fewer than three points are provided, combinations produces no triples and the method returns zero.
Complexity: There are O(n³) triples and constant work per triple, so time is O(n³) and auxiliary space is O(1) beyond the iterator.

Task and constraints: Compute the maximum triangle area from any three points.
Idea: Iterate over all ordered index triples with i<j<k and evaluate the shoelace determinant.
Technique and why it applies: The determinant's absolute value divided by two equals the triangle's area. result retains the largest value found.
Invariant: result is the maximum area among all triples processed up to the current indices.
Edge cases: Collinear triples contribute zero, and fewer than three points return zero. The formula works with negative coordinates as well.
Complexity: The three nested loops take O(n³) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Task and constraints: Partition an array into at most k groups to maximize the sum of each group's average.
Idea: Initialize suffix averages, then improve each DP entry by considering a first group ending at each possible boundary.
Technique and why it applies: dp[i] starts as the average of A[i:]. For each additional allowed group, the code compares that value with the average of A[i:j+1] plus dp[j+1].
Invariant: dp[i] is intended to store the best sum of averages for a suffix using the currently permitted number of groups.
Edge cases: The inner range excludes some boundaries and dp has only one dimension, making its overwritten states hard to interpret; correctness depends on the iteration order. The variable sum shadows the built-in.
Complexity: The nested loops take O(k n²) time and O(n) space.

Task and constraints: Find the minimum buses needed to travel from source stop to target stop.
Idea: Build a stop-to-bus index and run breadth-first search over reachable stops.
Technique and why it applies: Each bus route connects all its stops, and boarding a new bus increments the count. The seen_buses set prevents re-expanding the same route.
Invariant: bfs contains stops paired with the number of buses used to reach them.
Edge cases: The imports are nested in the class body, so names may resolve as class attributes rather than local globals; unqualified defaultdict/deque inside the method can raise NameError. There is also suspicious indentation around the target check in the supplied code.
Complexity: A corrected route-index BFS is O(total route stops) time and space; this snippet may not parse due to indentation.

Task and constraints: Compute the minimum number of bus routes needed to get from S to T.
Idea: Build a map from each stop to the routes that serve it, then explore reachable stops by bus-count layers.
Technique and why it applies: Each iteration expands one additional bus ride. lookup avoids revisiting stops, and routes serving a stop are explored to discover their other stops.
Invariant: q contains stops reachable using the current number of buses, and result is the next bus count.
Edge cases: The code removes route IDs from to_route[next_stop] while iterating over to_route[stop]; this mutation is on another set and is safe for distinct stop keys, but may prune route reuse globally.
Complexity: Each route-stop incidence is processed a bounded number of times, yielding near O(total route stops) time and space.

Task and constraints: Generate all valid coordinate pairs represented by a digit string enclosed in parentheses.
Idea: Split the digits into left and right parts and generate valid integer or decimal forms for each side.
Technique and why it applies: Leading zeros are disallowed for multi-digit integer parts, and fractional parts cannot end in zero. Cartesian products combine every valid left representation with every valid right representation.
Invariant: _splitToNums returns the valid representations for one fixed digit substring.
Edge cases: re and itertools are used without imports in the snippet. The regex pattern includes slash delimiters as if it were JavaScript, so Python re.match will not behave as intended for detecting all-zero strings.
Complexity: The number of outputs can be quadratic in split choices; work is proportional to generated coordinate pairs plus their string lengths.

Task and constraints: Return every valid decimal coordinate pair that can be formed from the digit string inside parentheses.
Idea: Enumerate each split between x and y, then generate valid integer/decimal representations for each side.
Technique and why it applies: Leading-zero and trailing-zero rules filter invalid forms; itertools.product combines all valid choices for the two coordinates.
Invariant: make(S,i,n) yields the permitted formats for one digit substring.
Edge cases: Empty fractional parts are permitted, representing integers. The code assumes the input has surrounding parentheses and a valid digit string.
Complexity: Generation time is proportional to the number and total lengths of returned pairs; auxiliary iterator state is small.

Task and constraints: Find the minimum number of instructions to move a race car from position zero to target.
Idea: Run breadth-first search over position and speed states, generating accelerate and reverse actions.
Technique and why it applies: Acceleration changes position by speed and doubles speed; reversal preserves position and changes speed to ±1. BFS explores instruction sequences in increasing length.
Invariant: Each queue layer contains states reachable in the same number of instructions, represented by steps.
Edge cases: The queue uses pop(0), which shifts a Python list. The reversal condition's boolean precedence is non-obvious, and there is no visited set, so repeated states may cause huge exploration.
Complexity: Without visited-state pruning, the search can grow exponentially and may not finish efficiently; queue storage can also grow exponentially.

Task and constraints: Compute the shortest instruction sequence that drives the race car to target.
Idea: Use dynamic programming by target distance, considering exact acceleration runs and sequences that reverse once or twice.
Technique and why it applies: For each i, bit_length gives the acceleration run length k. If 2^k-1 equals i, k instructions suffice; otherwise the recurrence considers overshooting or stopping short before reversing.
Invariant: dp[i] stores the minimum instructions needed to reach position i from the start with speed +1.
Edge cases: The recurrence references only smaller nonnegative positions in its transitions. target=0 returns dp[0]=0.
Complexity: The outer loop is O(target) and each state considers O(log target) values of j, giving O(target log target) time and O(target) space.

Task and constraints: Find the most frequent word in a paragraph after ignoring punctuation and excluding banned words.
Idea: Remove punctuation, lowercase the text, count words, and discard banned entries.
Technique and why it applies: Counter records frequencies; most_common(1) returns the word with highest count among remaining words.
Invariant: para_count holds the frequencies of normalized paragraph words not yet removed as banned.
Edge cases: The class imports string and Counter as class attributes; method-local name resolution may not find them as bare globals, so this snippet can raise NameError. If every word is banned, most_common(1)[0] also fails.
Complexity: Normalization and counting are O(n) time and O(U) space for U distinct words.

Task and constraints: Return the most frequent non-banned word in a paragraph, ignoring case and common punctuation.
Idea: Lowercase and split the paragraph, count stripped words, and scan for the highest-frequency word not banned.
Technique and why it applies: Counter aggregates occurrences; a set makes banned-word checks efficient. The scan updates result only for a strictly higher count, preserving the first encountered word on ties.
Invariant: result is the best eligible word seen so far under the iteration order of counts.
Edge cases: strip removes punctuation only from word ends, not punctuation embedded inside words. If every token is banned or no tokens exist, result remains the empty string.
Complexity: Counting and scanning take O(n) expected time and O(U) space.

Task and constraints: Find the minimum length of a reference string encoding all words as suffixes followed by a delimiter.
Idea: Build a trie of reversed unique words and sum lengths for words ending at leaf nodes.
Technique and why it applies: Reversing words makes shared suffixes share trie prefixes. A word that ends at a non-leaf is a suffix of a longer word and needs no separate encoding.
Invariant: Each trie node represents a reversed prefix, and tail_nodes records terminal nodes with each word's length plus delimiter.
Edge cases: Duplicate words are removed before insertion. A word that's a suffix of another ends at a non-leaf and is omitted from the total.
Complexity: Building the trie is O(total characters) expected time and space.

Task and constraints: Compute the shortest reference encoding length for a list of words using suffix sharing.
Idea: Insert reversed unique words into a trie and count lengths only for terminal words whose trie nodes have no children.
Technique and why it applies: A shorter word that is a suffix of a longer word ends at an internal node, so it is already represented in the longer word's encoding.
Invariant: nodes[i] points to the trie node reached by the reversed form of words[i].
Edge cases: Duplicate words are removed with set before trie construction. reduce and functools are imported redundantly; empty words would make reduce fail on an empty reversed iterator.
Complexity: Trie construction and final summation take O(total characters) expected time and space.

Task and constraints: For each position in s, return the distance to the nearest occurrence of character c.
Idea: Collect all positions of c and compare each index against every occurrence.
Technique and why it applies: The minimum absolute index difference is exactly the nearest-character distance.
Invariant: min_d is reset for each position and becomes the smallest distance found among all c positions.
Edge cases: If c never occurs, ch is empty and every position incorrectly receives len(s), rather than an explicitly defined sentinel. Empty s returns an empty list.
Complexity: With n characters and q occurrences of c, time is O(nq), worst-case O(n²), and space is O(n).

Task and constraints: Return each character's distance to the nearest occurrence of C.
Idea: Make a forward and backward pass, tracking the most recent matching position.
Technique and why it applies: The forward pass accounts for nearest matches on the left; the reverse pass accounts for matches on the right. Taking the minimum combines both directions.
Invariant: prev stores the latest matching index encountered in the current scan direction.
Edge cases: Initializing prev to -len(S) keeps the first forward distance large, while the reverse pass replaces it with right-side distances. If C never appears, results remain len(S).
Complexity: Two passes take O(n) time and O(n) output space.
